instruction: Generate a Playwright test to log in a user with email and password
input:
URL: https://taskflow-client-test.vercel.app Credentials: farid@gmail.com / 12345678 DOM Structure:
Test Intent: Verify that a user can successfully authenticate with valid credentials and be redirected to the dashboard
output:
# Strategy 1: Try using exact ID selectors
email_input = page.locator('#email-input')
email_input.wait_for(timeout=5000)
email_input.fill('farid@gmail.com')

password_input = page.locator('#password-input')
password_input.wait_for(timeout=5000)
password_input.fill('12345678')

submit_button = page.locator('#submit-btn')
submit_button.wait_for(timeout=5000)
submit_button.click()

# Assert that the user is redirected to the dashboard
try:
    page.wait_for_url('**/dashboard', timeout=10000)
    assert 'dashboard' in page.url
except Exception as e:
    console_errors.append(f'Failed to redirect to dashboard: {e}')
    raise

# Assert that a welcome message is visible
try:
    welcome = page.get_by_text('Welcome')
    welcome.wait_for(timeout=5000)
    assert welcome.is_visible()
except Exception as e:
    page_text = page.content()
    if 'Welcome' in page_text:
        print('DEBUG: Welcome text found on page but selector failed')
    else:
        print('DEBUG: Welcome text not found on page')
    raise Exception(f'Welcome message not visible: {e}')

instruction: Create a new project with name and description
input:
URL: https://taskflow-client-test.vercel.app/projects
User is already authenticated and logged in
Action: Create project named 'Website Redesign' with description 'Redesign the marketing website homepage'
DOM Structure:
<button id="new-project-btn" class="btn-primary">+ New Project</button>
<dialog id="project-modal" open>
  <form id="project-form">
    <input id="project-name" type="text" name="name" placeholder="Project Name" maxlength="100" />
    <textarea id="project-desc" name="description" placeholder="Description (optional)" maxlength="500"></textarea>
    <button type="submit" id="create-btn">Create Project</button>
    <button type="button" id="cancel-btn">Cancel</button>
  </form>
</dialog>

Test Intent: Verify new project is created and appears at the top of the project list
output:
# Click new project button with fallback strategy
selectors_to_try = [
    lambda: page.locator('#new-project-btn'),
    lambda: page.get_by_text('New Project'),
    lambda: page.get_by_role('button', name='New Project'),
]

new_btn = None
for selector_fn in selectors_to_try:
    try:
        elem = selector_fn()
        elem.wait_for(timeout=3000)
        if elem.is_visible():
            new_btn = elem
            break
    except:
        continue

if not new_btn:
    raise Exception('Could not find New Project button')

new_btn.click()
page.wait_for_timeout(500)  # Wait for modal to appear

# Fill project name
name_input = page.locator('#project-name')
name_input.wait_for(timeout=5000)
name_input.fill('Website Redesign')

# Fill description
desc_input = page.locator('#project-desc')
desc_input.wait_for(timeout=5000)
desc_input.fill('Redesign the marketing website homepage')

# Submit form
submit_btn = page.locator('#create-btn')
submit_btn.wait_for(timeout=5000)
submit_btn.click()

# Verify project was created
try:
    project_text = page.get_by_text('Website Redesign')
    project_text.wait_for(timeout=5000)
    assert project_text.is_visible()
    console_errors.append('Project created successfully')
except Exception as e:
    raise Exception(f'Project not found after creation: {e}')

instruction: Filter tasks by status in progress
input:
URL: https://taskflow-client-test.vercel.app/tasks?projectId=abc123 Project has 15 total tasks: 5 To Do, 7 In Progress, 3 Done User wants to see only In Progress tasks DOM Structure:
Task Title 1
Task Title 2
Test Intent: Verify that filtering works and only shows tasks with In Progress status
output:
# Select filter dropdown
filter_dropdown = page.locator('#status-filter')
filter_dropdown.wait_for(timeout=5000)
filter_dropdown.select_option('in_progress')

# Wait for filtering to complete
page.wait_for_timeout(1000)

# Verify only In Progress tasks are shown
task_items = page.locator('[data-status="in_progress"]')
task_count = task_items.count()

try:
    assert task_count > 0, 'No In Progress tasks found after filtering'
    print(f'Found {task_count} In Progress tasks')
except AssertionError as e:
    console_errors.append(f'Filtering failed: {e}')
    raise

# Verify no other status tasks are visible
all_visible_tasks = page.locator('.task-item:visible').count()
assert all_visible_tasks == task_count, f'Expected {task_count} tasks but found {all_visible_tasks}'

# Check each visible task has correct status
for i in range(task_count):
    status = task_items.nth(i).get_attribute('data-status')
    assert status == 'in_progress', f'Task {i} has status {status} instead of in_progress'

instruction: Edit an existing task's status from To Do to In Progress
input:
URL: https://taskflow-client-test.vercel.app/tasks/task-123 Task currently in To Do status DOM Structure:

Design homepage mockup

Test Intent: Verify task status can be updated and change is persisted
output:
# Open task detail page (already there)
# Get current status
current_status = page.locator('#status-dropdown')
current_status.wait_for(timeout=5000)

# Change status
current_status.select_option('in_progress')
page.wait_for_timeout(500)

# Verify the option was selected
selected_value = current_status.input_value()
assert selected_value == 'in_progress', f'Status not updated: {selected_value}'

# Save changes
save_btn = page.locator('#save-btn')
save_btn.wait_for(timeout=5000)
save_btn.click()

# Wait for save to complete
page.wait_for_timeout(1000)

# Verify status persisted
try:
    success_msg = page.get_by_text('Task updated')
    success_msg.wait_for(timeout=5000)
    assert success_msg.is_visible()
except Exception as e:
    # If no success message, check if status changed
    new_status = page.locator('#status-dropdown').input_value()
    assert new_status == 'in_progress', f'Status not persisted: {new_status}'
    
print('Task status updated successfully')

instruction: Verify overdue tasks are highlighted on dashboard
input:
URL: https://taskflow-client-test.vercel.app/dashboard Project has 3 tasks: 1. Task A - due 2026-09-01 - status To Do (OVERDUE) 2. Task B - due 2026-09-15 - status In Progress (NOT overdue) 3. Task C - due 2026-09-01 - status Done (NOT marked overdue even though past due) DOM Structure:
Task A OVERDUE
Task B
Task C
Test Intent: Verify overdue highlighting follows the rule: due_date < today AND status != Done
output:
import time
from datetime import datetime

# Get current date
today = datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')

# Find all task cards
task_cards = page.locator('.task-card')
task_count = task_cards.count()

print(f'Found {task_count} task cards')

# Check each task
for i in range(task_count):
    card = task_cards.nth(i)
    task_id = card.get_attribute('data-task-id')
    due_date = card.get_attribute('data-due')
    status = card.get_attribute('data-status')
    
    # Determine if should be overdue
    should_be_overdue = due_date < today and status != 'done'
    
    # Check if has overdue badge
    has_overdue_badge = False
    try:
        badge = card.locator('.badge.overdue')
        has_overdue_badge = badge.is_visible()
    except:
        pass
    
    # Assert
    try:
        assert has_overdue_badge == should_be_overdue, \
            f'Task {task_id}: due={due_date}, status={status}, should_be_overdue={should_be_overdue}, has_badge={has_overdue_badge}'
    except AssertionError as e:
        console_errors.append(str(e))
        raise
    
    print(f'✓ Task {task_id}: overdue badge correct')

print('All overdue highlighting rules verified')
